name: Somasambhu
dates_notes: Usually placed in the late eleventh century; later Śaiva manuals cite and adapt his ritual synthesis.
core_thesis: Somaśambhu's *Kriyākāṇḍakramāvalī* is a major Sanskrit Śaiva Siddhānta synthesis of ritual procedure. It treats regular, occasional, and goal-directed rites, including initiation, consecration, and installation, within a Śaiva theological order. The work's historical importance is not a claim that ritual is philosophically secondary: it is a key witness to the way Siddhānta integrated doctrine, initiation, and temple or domestic practice. Later manuals drew extensively on it.

engaged_works.title: Kriyakandakramavali
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely transmitted as Somaśambhu's ritual manual; later commentary and manuscript traditions also call it the *Somaśambhupaddhati*.
engaged_works.summary: A large Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual that orders daily worship, initiation, installation, expiation, and related procedures. It has received a multi-volume critical edition, translation, and annotation, but no verified local primary-text witness is linked here.
